hook.text: Bronze medalists are happier than silver medalists. Silver thinks 'almost gold.' Bronze thinks 'I almost got nothing.'

buildup.text: Social comparison is automatic. Your brain evaluates your status relative to others, not in absolute terms.

discovery.text: Festinger's social comparison theory shows upward comparison kills joy even when your situation is objectively great.

twist.text: Instagram shows everyone's highlights. You compare your insides to their outsides—a rigged game that makes you lose.

climax.text: Studies link heavy social media use to lower life satisfaction. The joy thief isn't your life—it's the comparison.

punchline.text: Joy doesn't survive comparison. It was never meant to.

quiz.question: Why are bronze medalists often happier than silver medalists?
options: They compare downward to getting nothing
